source_document.body:
2026 SEMA Show • Mitsubishi Returns to Las Vegas With the Fresh 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition
106-Mile Ferrari F50 Becomes the Most Expensive Ever at $18M, Breaks Two-Month Record by $4M
24 photos
Photo: Broad Arrow
Forget the tired tourism slogan claiming what happens in Sin City stays there, because when $92,800,000 worth of exotic metal and carbon fiber changes hands in 24 hours, the noise echoes all the way to Maranello. On October 31, 2026, Broad Arrow Auctions turned the Wynn Las Vegas into a scene straight out of Ocean's Eleven, except the billionaires were robbing their own bank accounts for a royal flush of Ferraris, led by the lowest-mileage Ferrari F50 ever. And, as of that same day, the most expensive in the world.
The Vegas showdown was basically a Ferrari tour de force, with five of the top ten best-sellers coming with a prancing horsey on the nose. In fact, the first four cars were all Ferraris (F50, Daytona SP2, La Ferrari, and Enzo), with a Bugatti Chiron Super Sport daring to take fifth, at a paltry $4.57 million, inching ahead of the 599 SA Aperta.
Staged beside the Concours at Wynn Las Vegas, the standing-room-only spectacle saw auctioneer Thomas Forrester work the room like Frank Sinatra at the Sands. Bidders pushed the F50 to a $17,000,000 hammer price before fees landed it at its record-shattering figure. Still, it failed to meet the $20,000,000 estimate.
With bidder registrations up 63 percent, and 76 percent of lots sold, 10 world records fell during the highest-grossing Las Vegas car auction in history. Surpsingly, the hypercars of the 2010s, like the Koenigsegg Regera and Mclaren P1 GTR, had to settle for the second half of the Top Ten Billboard. The Broad Arrow Vegas show was basically a “Ferrari versus The World” musical.
Photo: Broad Arrow Of the 64 cars that were sold (out of 84 offered), 33 came from Maranello – every other car was a Ferrari. Maranello fever practically melted the casino chandeliers as modern prancing horses hijacked the leaderboard. Right behind the $18,705,000 F50, a 2025 Ferrari Daytona SP3 hammered to a non-charity world record of $18,540,000. Flipping horsepower beats playing blackjack.
Meanwhile, a 2014 Ferrari LaFerrari pulled in $8,805,000, and the ultra-rare 2011 Ferrari 599 SA Aperta casually strolled off with $4,350,000. It was about as close as you’d get to a middle-east petrodollar wedding, with money flying around like exotic birds and expensive apple juice corks (no alcohol where the oil overflows).
So what makes this specific 1997 Ferrari F50 worth the GDP of a small island nation? Built as the 334th example out of only 349 units produced between 1995 and 1997, this late-production treasure was one of the 25 cars originally delivered to the United Kingdom. Dressed in classic Rosso Corsa paint over Nero leather with Rosso cloth seat inserts, it wears just 106 miles, or 170 km, from new.
Photo: Broad Arrow Across 29 years - which means previous caretakers drove this masterpiece an average of 3.6 miles, or 5.8 km, annually, exercising the superhuman restraint of a monk at a Las Vegas buffet. If they ever drove it at all – this car may have very well gathered those miles from being pushed around in service shops.
Because nobody ever actually went anywhere in it, the car retains its removable hardtop, factory flight case, fitted Schedoni luggage set, unworn driving shoes, and complete tool kit, costing the buyer $176,462 per mile. Virgin Galactic space trips are probably public transportation, by comparison.
To grasp why wealthy collectors treat the F50 moniker like the biblical manger with license plates, put time on pause, then rewind to 1995. Ferrari unveiled the F50 at the Geneva Motor Show to celebrate its 50th anniversary, arriving two full years ahead of the actual 1997 milestone because Italian passion doesn’t do calendars. Following the 288 GTO and twin-turbocharged F40, Maranello ditched forced induction to build a road-legal Formula 1 car for purists.
Photo: Broad Arrow That Formula 1 claim was not marketing fluff cooked up over espresso. Bolted directly to the rear bulkhead of the carbon-fiber monocoque tub as a fully stressed chassis member sits the Tipo F130B 4.7-liter naturally aspirated V12 engine. Derived from the 3.5-liter V12 that powered Alain Prost’s 1990 Ferrari 641 to 6 Grand Prix victories, this 60-valve masterpiece features 5 valves per cylinder and titanium connecting rods.
Three intakes, two exhausts – and you can imagine what those heads look like without the valves. Swiss cheese is the closest thing, but those quintuple taps moved air and fuel (crude or burnt) like nothing before.
Breathing through variable-length intake runners, the 286.7-cubic-inch powerplant unleashes 513 hp, (520 PS), at 8,000 rpm and 347 lb-ft (471 Nm), of torque at 6,500 rpm, shrieking like an operatic banshee to an 8,500 rpm redline. Weighing just 2,712 lbs (1,230 kg) dry, the Pininfarina-styled roadster rockets from 0 to 60 mph, or 97 kph, in 3.8 seconds on its way to 202 mph / 325 kph. That’s basic supercar performance today.
Photo: Broad Arrow While modern hypercars coddle drivers with stability control modes named after video games, the F50 offers a 6-speed gated manual gearbox, pushrod suspension with inboard electronically controlled Bilstein dampers, and zero electronic mercy . There is no power steering, no power brake booster, and no anti-lock brakes.
Ironically, that uncompromising brutality made the F50 the awkward middle child in 2016, when examples traded between $1,500,000 and $2,500,000 behind the 1,311-unit F40.
Over the past 10 years, however, the collector market experienced a rude awakening as silent batteries and dual-clutch paddles conquered the showroom floor. Realizing Maranello would never again pair a naturally aspirated V12 with a 3-pedal open gate in a flagship, buyers stampeded. Over the last 6 years, Hagerty condition #2 valuations skyrocketed by 352 percent, while standard European market averages doubled from €2,500,000 in 2022 to €5,000,000 in 2026.
Photo: Broad Arrow Then came 2026, a year when the F50 market drank rocket fuel and condition #2 values surged another 102 percent. Including Las Vegas, 7 of the 10 highest F50 auction prices ever recorded happened in 2026. January saw RM Sotheby’s sell 2 examples for $8,800,000 and $8,740,000, while Mecum Kissimmee moved two 1995 cars for $12,110,000 and $12,210,000, including a 252-mile, or 405 km, specimen that briefly looked wildly expensive.
After another 1995 example brought $9,790,000 in May 2026, a Giallo Modena 1996 F50 showing 4,660 miles, or 7,500 km, hit $14,575,000 at Mecum Monterey on August 15, 2026. Barely two months later, Broad Arrow’s 106-mile time capsule obliterated that benchmark by $4,130,000.
This year is most probably going to close with this $18M high note, but there is one Ferrari F50 coming up next January, at the Mecum Kissimmee. It once belonged to the Sultan of Brunei, and I wonder if this record will hold for long. Commentators may ask if we are witnessing a collector car bubble, but in Sin City, the house always wins, and the house drives a 1997 Ferrari F50. source_document.body:
BMW is saying goodbye to the iX. With the 2026 model essentially sold out, BMW is preparing to introduce its replacement, which already looks like a big upgrade.
BMW iX sells out as the iX5 steps in
The iX went on sale in the US in 2022 as BMW’s first dedicated electric SUV. After a short four-year run, BMW confirmed earlier this year that it was discontinuing the iX in the US after the 2026 model year to make room for its next-generation of fully electric vehicles.
BMW didn’t take long to sell through inventory, with 2026 iX models essentially sold out in the US.
The iX landing page now redirects you to the new BMW X5 instead. According to online auto research firm CarsDirect , about 10 new iX models remain nationwide.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
BMW’s Neue Klasse vehicles, starting with the new 2027 iX3, mark a step change from its previous EVs.
At the center is the Neue Klasse platform, which introduces BMW’s sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive, new batteries, and an 800-volt electrical architecture.
2026 BMW iX xDrive60 (Source: BMW)
BMW said the new Gen6 eDrive system delivers 30% higher charging speeds and driving range than its previous system, with some models seeing an even greater increase.
The 2027 iX3 50 xDrive , BMW’s first Neue Klasse vehicle, starts at $61,500 and offers an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 434 miles. In comparison, the 2026 iX xDrive 60 had an EPA range of up to 364 miles.
BMW iX5 60 xDrive M Sport Package (Source: BMW)
While the iX3 is a smaller, compact electric SUV compared to the iX, BMW is preparing to launch the iX5 as a more direct replacement.
The gas-powered 2027 X5 40 xDrive is now on sale, starting at $72,100, but BMW is expected to launch the electric iX5 in early 2027.
A few weeks ago, BMW put the new iX5 60 xDrive to the test at an international media event in Southern California to show just how fast it can charge.
BMW iX5 60 xDrive hits 460 kW (Source: BMW)
During the event, the new iX5 hit a peak of 464 kW. BMW said that with up to 460 kW peak charging, the iX5 60 xDrive can add up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes. To charge the battery from 10% to 80% takes just 22 minutes.
Using a 144 kWh battery, BMW said the electric SUV will offer up to an estimated 435 miles of range on a single charge.
BMW iX5 60 xDrive interior with M Sport Package (Source: BMW)
The iX5 is powered by a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain, delivering a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque. BMW says it can go from 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds and tow up to 6,000 lbs.
Inside, the iX5 will be an upgrade from the iX, adopting BMW’s Neue Klasse design. The setup includes a 17.9″ navigation touchscreen and the new BMW Panoramic Vision that spans the windshield. You can also opt to add the optional 14.6″ passenger screen for a third display.
BMW iX5 60 xDrive interior with M Sport Package (Source: BMW)
Measuring 197.2″ long, 78.7″ wide, and 68.9″ tall, the iX5 is slightly longer and taller than the outgoing iX, with more of a traditional SUV design.
BMW is expected to open orders for the new iX5 60 xDrive this month, starting at $79,800, with a full launch in early 2027. It will be BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US.
Production is set to begin at BMW’s Plant Spartanburg in South Carolina by the end of the year, with the first deliveries expected in early 2027.

source_document.body:
Truckload carrier Pamt Corp. lost money again during the third quarter. Like other carriers , it pointed to elevated driver procurement costs and the spike in diesel fuel prices as the culprits.
Pamt ( NASDAQ: PAMT ) reported a net loss of $8.1 million, or 38 cents per share, on Monday after the market closed.
Earnings-per-share headwinds in the period included a $3.7-million year-over-year decline in gains on equipment sales (14 cents per share), and a $3.2-million y/y decline in non-operating income (12 cents per share). (The non-operating income line captures the change in value of its stock portfolio.)
Pamt booked a net loss of 27 cents per share in the year-ago quarter.
Pamt President Lance Stewart said that while the company is “aligning customer rates with the inflationary cost increases experienced over the past four years,” the “cumulative cost increases continue to outpace the pricing improvements achieved to date.”
Consolidated revenue increased 8% y/y to $163 million. Revenue was up just 2% excluding fuel surcharges.
Table: Pamt’s key performance indicators
Truckload revenue (ex-fuel) was flat y/y as a 3% decline in average trucks was mostly offset by a 1.4% increase in revenue per truck per week. Loaded miles per truck increased 4% y/y in the quarter. Revenue per loaded mile (ex-fuel) was down 1% y/y, but up 11% from the second quarter .
The third quarter marked 12 straight operating losses for the TL unit. It recorded a 109.1% operating ratio (ex-fuel), 240 basis points worse y/y.
SONAR: Van Contract Rate Per Mile Index ( VCRPM1.USA ) for 2026 (blue shaded area), 2025 (yellow line), 2024 (green line) and 2023 (pink line). The index shows a 7-day moving average of the initial reporting of dry van contract rates without fuel or accessorial charges. To learn more about SONAR, click here .
The logistics unit reported $45 million in revenue, a 7% y/y increase, and a 92.6% OR, 650 bps better y/y.
(Pamt doesn’t provide gross profit margins for the unit, nor operating metrics like load counts and revenue per load.)
Pamt used $18 million in operating cash flow in the first nine months of the year. Liquidity (cash, equity holdings and availability on its line of credit) of $102 million was $15 million lower than in the second quarter. Outstanding debt was down $10 million to $323 million.
“While I am disappointed that the progress achieved in customer pricing was offset by these cost pressures, I am encouraged by the continued sequential improvement in our operating performance,” said Stewart. “I remain confident that our ongoing initiatives, combined with improving market conditions, will contribute to stronger financial results as we move forward.”
Why it matters? Pamt’s results show fleets are having difficulties addressing multiple years of cost inflation, which occurred alongside weak pricing.

Photo: bp pulse
EV drivers have another way to charge at bp pulse without adding its app to their phones. The network has joined ChargeHub’s Passport Hub, connecting more than 850 charging points at over 95 US locations to ChargeHub and participating charging services and automakers.
Drivers can find, access, and pay for bp pulse charging through ChargeHub or participating services connected to Passport Hub.
Passport Hub handles the connections between charging networks and the services drivers use, including exchanging session information and settling payments. That lets a charging operator connect to multiple services through a single integration.
In practice, ChargeHub users can pull up a bp pulse location, select a port, and start charging from their existing account. The app displays the charging cost and wallet balance, and drivers need funds in their ChargeHub wallet to begin charging.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
ChargeHub also shows real-time charger availability and lets drivers filter by connector type. Its bp pulse guide says most of the network’s chargers use CCS, with a growing share offering NACS.
Meanwhile, bp pulse has been adding physical charging sites, too. Recent openings include 12 charging bays at a TravelCenters of America location in Grand Bay, Alabama, and 22 bays near Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport.
Before starting a session, check the price shown in the app. ChargeHub’s guide notes that its Plus subscription waives activation fees, so using an existing account doesn’t necessarily mean paying the same total as another payment method.
